decisions.reason: The address autocomplete web service is a low-cost extension of the firm's own databases, and with the firm expanding and holding slack there is no shortfall to trigger search for other uses of its resources.

The Austrian gas grid fee database sits close to the core grid-fee data business and fits the platform strategy, though its smaller foreign market makes it somewhat more exposed if results disappoint.
Peak load window determination is a regulated network-operator process that matches the firm's core competence and likely meets aspirations as a recurring service.
The end-customer tariff database is a multi-model product line central to the firm's market data business, so dropping it is unlikely while the firm is growing.
Custom web services are a flexible offering that supports the move toward SaaS and standardized data exchange, with little fixed cost to justify cutting it.
The postal code lookup service is a cheap byproduct of the existing data assets, and slack from expansion allows the firm to carry it even if its results are uncertain.
